reviewMethod: Same assistant visually compared each selected original Problems PNG and corresponding Solutions PNG after committing all first attempts. No OCR, separate model inference, or independent adjudicator.

cases.keyResult: 4 cm from the foot of A (16 cm from the foot of B)
cases.review: Reflection construction and result agree. This familiar geometry was already identified as potentially exposed in the first attempt.
Equivalent to the first attempt after renaming launch speed u/v. The first attempt also retains the nonnegative-time existence condition; native optics does not implement the projectile problem.

The solution uses the opposite Cartesian sign convention, so its signed radius -20/3 m is not a physical disagreement. Its initial 'u=-25 m' line is inconsistent with the question and its own subsequent use of -2.5 m; treat that line as a source typographical error, not a new input.

cases.keyResult: Final apparent image 7.5 cm below the water surface
cases.review: Matches first answer, equivalently 22.5 cm above the mirror pole. The internal real focus and final emergent virtual image must remain distinct.

cases.keyResult: Solution uses a 2 m ceiling height and gives shadow radius 845/3 cm; limiting ring radius about 0.23 m
cases.review: The supplied Problems image explicitly states 2 cm, while the Solutions diagram and equation use 2 m=200 cm. The frozen first answer 53/3 cm follows the actual problem. For the solution's altered height the same equation gives 845/3 cm. The limit a=60/sqrt(7) cm agrees; finite elevated-ceiling intersection requires a strictly below this bound.

cases.keyResult: 157.2 degrees in air and 128.4 degrees in water, keeping internal angle 30 degrees in each medium
cases.review: First answer agrees with the key's reflecting/equilateral/minimum-reset interpretation. The accurate water result is 128.45773265562514 degrees (128.5 to one decimal); the key gets 128.4 by rounding incidence to 34.2 before doubling. The question's failure to specify whether incidence is readjusted on immersion remains a real ambiguity. The unchanged-incidence alternative is preserved, not silently replaced.

cases.keyResult: Final image at the pole of the silvered rear surface
cases.review: Same as first answer x=+r relative to centre, virtual after final emergence. The key changes radius symbol r to R in its last equation but its geometric conclusion agrees.

Both real and virtual branches in the first answer agree with the solution. Passing this manual inverse calculation through a separately supplied forward focal length would not turn it into an engine inverse solve.

cases.keyResult: Refractive index 4/3 under the thin-lens-in-air convention
cases.review: Matches first answer. The first answer correctly labels the thin/paraxial and air assumptions rather than treating an ideal lens as a measured material.

cases.keyResult: Longitudinal chromatic aberration 0.032 m; dispersive power approximately 0.0325 using sqrt(f_red*f_blue)
cases.review: Focal separation agrees exactly. The first attempt explicitly used arithmetic mean focal length 0.984 m, while the key uses geometric mean sqrt(0.968) m. They give 0.0325203252 and 0.0325246251 respectively, both 0.0325 at the stated precision. Record the convention correction in this review only. Neither supplies an independently stated reference wavelength for an exact material dispersive power.

interpretation: Seven straightforward key agreements, one conflicting source unit, one conditional/rounding agreement, one approximation-convention difference. Not a ten-out-of-ten accuracy score, and none is a native simulation result.
nextPriority: Propose a bounded reduced-facts inverse-query layer for reflection point, thin lens magnification and curved mirror magnification. Keep mixed refracting/reflecting geometry and continuous-visibility queries separate; this evaluation does not authorize new physics.
